title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 4th District
area: Orange, Durham and Chatham counties, including Chapel Hill and Durham.

context.text: Incumbent Valerie Foushee (D) won her Democratic primary and faces Mahesh Ganorkar (R) and Guy Meilleur (L), both of whom advanced from canceled Republican and Libertarian primaries respectively, in the general election.

candidates.name: Valerie Foushee

summary.text: Valerie Foushee is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 4th Congressional District. A Chapel Hill native, she worked for the Chapel Hill Police Department for 21 years and held local office on the school board and Orange County Board of Commissioners before serving in the state legislature. She was elected to Congress in 2022 and serves on the Science, Space, and Technology and Transportation and Infrastructure committees.

background.text: Born in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, in 1956. According to her official biography, she grew up in Chapel Hill as the oldest of six children of parents who had left high school to raise the family.

Attended the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill for two years before withdrawing for financial reasons; returned and graduated in 2008 with a bachelor's degree in political science and Afro and African-American studies.
Joined the Chapel Hill Police Department as an administrative officer in 1987 and retired in 2008 after 21 years; also held administrative positions with insurance and research companies.
Served on the Chapel Hill-Carrboro City school board from 1997 to 2004 (chair 2001-2003).
Served on the Orange County Board of Commissioners from 2004 to 2012 (chair 2008-2010); her official biography says she was the first African American woman to chair the commission.
Served in the North Carolina General Assembly: District 50 in the House in 2013, then District 23 in the State Senate from 2013 to 2023, succeeding Eleanor Kinnaird.

Won the Democratic primary for the open 4th District seat in May 2022 and the November 2022 general election; her official biography says she is the first African American and first woman to represent the district. Renominated in the March 3, 2026 Democratic primary over Nida Allam and Mary Patterson.

Serves on the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee (Ranking Member of the Space and Aeronautics Subcommittee; Energy Subcommittee) and the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee (Aviation and Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees).

priorities.text: Delivering relief to working families facing higher costs, including offsetting the impact of tariffs on everyday expenses.
Government oversight and accountability, including of U.S. military assistance abroad and immigration enforcement agencies.

positions.summary: Introduced the American Tariff Rebate Act to send direct tax rebates to middle-class families to offset the cost of the President's tariffs.
positions.quote: The American Tariff Rebate Act puts money directly back into the pockets of middle-class families by providing swift, direct tax rebates to offset the costs associated with the President's tariffs and the rising cost of everyday expenses.

positions.summary: Voted for an amendment to restrict U.S. military assistance to Israel, saying Congress must exercise oversight over how that assistance is provided.
positions.quote: Today, I supported Congressman Massie's amendment because Congress must exercise its oversight role and ensure accountability in how U.S. military assistance is provided.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, where she was ranking member of the Investigations and Oversight subcommittee in the 118th Congress.
Introduced the American Tariff Rebate Act, which would provide direct tax rebates to offset the cost of tariffs for middle-class families.

candidates.name: Mahesh Ganorkar
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Republican primary.

summary.text: Mahesh (Max) Ganorkar is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Valerie Foushee in North Carolina's 4th Congressional District. He holds an M.B.A. and has worked on U.S.-India business joint ventures and home design, and left his career to be a stay-at-home father. He previously ran in Republican congressional primaries in 2022 and 2024.

background.text: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey, described being born and brought up in a farming family, immigrating from a socialist country, and later living in New Jersey before moving to North Carolina.
Holds an M.B.A.; professional experience includes facilitating international joint ventures between U.S. and Indian companies and residential construction and home design.
Said on his 2024 campaign website that after his first child was born he decided to give up his career to be a stay-at-home dad; in his 2022 survey, he said he also home-schooled his three children.
Says his political activism began in 2009, when he founded a Tea Party group in New Jersey that he ran until his family moved to North Carolina.
Ran in the May 17, 2022 Republican primary for North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District, won by Christine Villaverde.
Ran in the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for North Carolina's 4th Congressional District, won by Eric Blankenburg with about 70 percent to Ganorkar's 30 percent.
Advanced as the 2026 Republican nominee after the March 3, 2026 primary for the 4th District was uncontested.

priorities.text: Repealing the Sixteenth Amendment and giving taxpayers more direct control over federal spending approvals through their tax filings.
Election security measures including mandatory voter ID, paper ballots, and eliminating mail-in and absentee voting.
Opposing illegal immigration, including mandatory E-Verify and ending birthright citizenship for children of people in the country illegally.

positions.summary: Says he will support and vow to protect the nation's borders, oppose sanctuary cities, and require mandatory E-Verify for employment and rental housing.
Proposes repealing the Sixteenth Amendment (which authorizes the federal income tax) and replacing it with a system where taxpayers directly approve federal spending.

candidates.researchNotes: Ganorkar has not held elected office; positions are drawn from his campaign website as quoted by Ballotpedia. He did not complete a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey.

candidates.name: Guy Meilleur
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Guy Meilleur is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 4th Congressional District. A consulting arborist and educator who lives in Durham, he has been a Libertarian candidate for the North Carolina House in 2022 and for this congressional seat in 2024.

background.text: According to his 2022 INDY Week questionnaire, grew up in south Chicago; his campaign website says he moved to North Carolina in 1985 to study trees under Dr. J.C. Raulston at North Carolina State University and has lived in Durham since 2015.

According to his campaign website, worked as a lecturer and curator at North Carolina State University, an instructor at Duke University, and an arborist at the University of North Carolina, and has taught in 29 countries.

Works as a consulting arborist (Historic Tree Care, per his 2022 questionnaire); says he served on the national tree care standards committee and wrote the industry standard for tree inspection, and co-presents the PuppetTREE educational shows.

Ran as the Libertarian candidate for North Carolina House District 30 in 2022 (about 12 percent in a race won by incumbent Marcia Morey) and for the 4th Congressional District in 2024, when incumbent Valerie Foushee won.
Advanced to the 2026 general election after the March 3, 2026 Libertarian primary was canceled.

candidates.researchNotes: No campaign website content, Candidate Connection survey, or public policy statements were located within the research budget; Ballotpedia's page for Meilleur contains no biography or issue statements beyond his election history.
